articles.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev was welcomed at an official ceremony in Muscat attended by Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, as he began a state visit to Oman. After Uzbekistan's national anthem was played, the leaders greeted members of the official delegations from both countries.

articles.title: The new Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina began its Mandate
articles.summary: The inaugural session of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina has concluded, during which the newly elected members of this institution officially assumed office. The new composition of the Presidency of BiH consists of Darijana Filipović (representing the Croat people), Željka Cvijanović (representing the Serb people), and Denis Bećirović (representing the Bosniak people).
articles.body: The inaugural session of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina has concluded, during which the newly elected members of this institution officially assumed office. The new composition of the Presidency of BiH consists of Darijana Filipović (representing the Croat people), Željka Cvijanović (representing the Serb people), and Denis Bećirović (representing the Bosniak people). Željka Cvijanović has secured a second consecutive term as a member of the Presidency of BiH. During the campaign, she stated that her priority for this second term would be to utilize political and constitutional mechanisms to—in her words—preserve the constitutional capacity, stability, and functionality of Republika Srpska, as well as to transfer competencies from the state level back to the entity level. This process began with decisions made by the National Assembly of Republika Srpska, which drew numerous reactions from the international community and its institutions. Cvijanović asserted that there would be no “rotten compromises” during this new term and indicated that she would maintain a coordinated stance with Darijana Filipović regarding the observance of constitutional mechanisms designed to protect the constituent peoples. As her first action following the inauguration, she announced a review of the diplomatic network. ŽELJKA CVIJANOVIĆ, Member of the Presidency of BiH (SNSD) “Sometimes you have to swallow the inclusion of a name that you firmly believe is harmful, just so the process can move forward. Now, the question arises: should we even stick to such an established rule—a rule that has, for many years, facilitated the abuse of diplomatic and consular practices and systems, and which has resulted in so much incorrect or misleading information being disseminated globally? A rule that has led to greater division rather than fostering a sense of mutual reliance? In short, everything needs to be discussed. I cannot tell you exactly what the outcome will look like, but these are matters that need to be defined.” Throughout her political career, Željka Cvijanović has held various positions, including those of Prime Minister and President of Republika Srpska. She studied English at the Faculty of Philosophy in Sarajevo and graduated from the Faculty of Philosophy in Banja Luka. She completed postgraduate studies in diplomatic and consular law in Banja Luka. She worked as an English language teacher and professor, as a senior translator, and subsequently as an assistant with the European Union Monitoring Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina. She was born in Teslić and lives in Banja Luka. She is 59 years old, married, and has two sons. Darijana Filipović is a new member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Her entry into the state leadership marks the return of the HDZ BiH (Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina) to the Presidency after eight years—specifically, following two consecutive terms served by Željko Komšić. She views her accession to the Presidency of BiH as both a major victory and a significant responsibility, noting that the people have made their choice regarding who they wish to represent them. During the campaign, she emphasized that it is time for equality to finally become the standard, highlighting the constitutional equality of the Croat people in BiH and the importance of legitimate political representation. She expressed a desire for the Presidency of BiH to cease being an institution associated with divisions, political blockages, and a “two-against-one” dynamic. Her primary focus will be on accelerating Bosnia and Herzegovina’s path toward European integration. Regarding NATO, she stated that the need for accession is clear from the perspective of the Croat people. In terms of foreign policy, she intends to work on strengthening relations between BiH and Croatia. The position of Chair of the Presidency of BiH is assumed on a rotational basis, automatically, every eight months; this means that each member will serve as Chair twice during their term. “We need a stable parliamentary majority. We have seen, even during this current term, that attempts to change the parliamentary majority often lead us all into an institutional deadlock—which benefits no one in terms of equality. A key priority is to try to find a permanent solution to the issue we also discussed during the campaign: ensuring that the position of the Croat member of the Presidency does not depend on electoral arithmetic, but rather is resolved through the Election Law. I believe these elections have shown that the present moment offers the right opportunity for this.” Darijana Filipović’s political career spans approximately 15 years and encompasses various levels of party and institutional work, without significant media exposure. She rose through the ranks of party structures in the Herzegovina-Neretva Canton. She served as a representative in the Federal Parliament, and subsequently in the State Parliament. She was born in Mostar, where she also graduated from the Faculty of Economics. She is 39 years old and married. Denis Bećirović has won a second consecutive term as a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. During his campaign, he emphasized the preservation and strengthening of state institutions, as well as opposition to policies that threaten the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. He called for citizens and political parties to unite around common state interests. He pledged that the rule of law and the fight against corruption would remain his enduring priorities. He stressed that the economic and general development of Bosnia and Herzegovina is inextricably linked to accelerating the path toward membership in the European Union and NATO. His focus was on creating conditions for citizens to remain in BiH, fostering economic progress, and providing support to the most vulnerable segments of the population. “There must be no changes to the strategic foreign policy direction of BiH. We must continue our path toward the EU, and we must continue our path toward NATO membership. We are a state that promotes good regional cooperation, and we must continue working in that direction. I also wish to send a message to the region: BiH is the greatest victim in the region. At the same time, BiH is the strongest advocate for cooperation, peace, and development. The future of our region lies not in adopting the Russian model of relations with neighbors, but in adopting the European model. A message to the EU: help BiH—the European Union and its values are also being defended here in BiH.” Denis Bećirović entered the political arena while still in high school. He has held numerous and diverse positions, serving as a representative in the Assembly of Tuzla Canton, and subsequently in both the federal and state parliaments—serving as both a representative and a delegate—over the course of three consecutive terms. He holds a PhD in History. He is the author of four books and numerous scholarly papers. He is 51 years old, married, and has two children.l, BHRT writes.

articles.title: Georgia Skips EU Ministerial on Connectivity, Citing Lower-Level Invitation
articles.summary: Georgian Foreign Ministry said Tbilisi would skip the EU connectivity ministerial in Brussels on November 16, citing the absence of an invitation “at an appropriate level,” while expressing commitment to “constructive cooperation” with the bloc. The meeting, held on the sidelines of the EU Foreign Affairs Council, brings together ministers from the South Caucasus, Central …
articles.body: Georgian Foreign Ministry said Tbilisi would skip the EU connectivity ministerial in Brussels on November 16, citing the absence of an invitation "at an appropriate level," while expressing commitment to "constructive cooperation" with the bloc. The meeting, held on the sidelines of the EU Foreign Affairs Council, brings together ministers from the South Caucasus, Central Asia, Moldova, Turkey and Ukraine, according to the EU's official announcement. Georgia was also absent from a similar meeting in Luxembourg last year, with the ministry at the time also citing a lower-level invitation as the reason for declining to attend. "Georgia has not received an invitation at the appropriate level to participate in the events planned in Brussels on November 16, including the Connectivity Ministerial. Accordingly, no Georgian representative will participate in the meeting," the Foreign Ministry said in the statement. The statement came a day after Georgian media outlet Publika cited Vakhtang Makharoblishvili, Georgian Ambassador to the EU, as confirming his participation in the meeting, following media reports that Georgia again received a lower-level invitation to the meeting. "At the same time, Georgia remains committed to constructive cooperation with the European Union and is ready to participate in meetings if invited at the appropriate level," the Ministry added, noting that "Brussels is aware of this position." Kos: We Invite, But Not on Highest Level Speaking at a news briefing on November 16, EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos told Deutsche Welle that Brussels has repeatedly invited Georgian representatives, but not at the highest level. "Now, for two or three times we have invited the representatives of Georgia to our events on connectivity, and they never came," Kos said. "So we try to engage, we invite them. They don't want to come. We don't invite on the highest level." "We are looking for the engagement; we wanted to have dialogue on the visa liberalization, it was not possible, so, I hope that the Foreign Affairs Council in January [...] will bring some movement," Kos added, referring to EU HR/VP Kaja Kallas' earlier announcement of a "deeper discussion with the foreign ministers regarding Georgia in January." 21/04/2026 - Kos: EU to Involve Georgia in Connectivity to Extent Tbilisi’s Willing to Engage ‘On Other Areas’ Separately, responding to a question from Euroscope, the commissioner said the EU doesn't want Georgia "excluded from these very important activities we do in the fields of trade, transport, energy and digital." Kos, however, said that, in this direction, too, "there are conditions." "We will invite them again and again," she said. "I believe that we have to be engaged. But of course they also have to deliver." Kobakhidze Expects 'Dignified Invitation' Meanwhile, Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze criticized the level of Georgia's invitation, reiterating his earlier calls for a "dignified invitation." "The Georgian people deserve a fair and healthy approach, which we do not see today," Kobakhidze told journalists during a November 16 press briefing. "Where our country receives a dignified invitation, it will be appropriately represented. Where we see a different attitude, we will respond accordingly." Commenting on Georgia's exclusion from the EU Enlargement Forum, Kobakhidze accused European officials of acting against Europe's interests, saying, "For us, this is further confirmation that the European bureaucracy is not acting in accordance with Europe's objective interests." The relations between Georgia, which became an EU candidate country in 2023, and Brussels worsened amid the Georgian Dream government’s anti-democratic moves and anti-EU discourse. The EU said in November 2025 that Georgia is a candidate country “in name only” and moved to suspend visa-free travel for Georgian holders of diplomatic and service passports. Brussels has also repeatedly stated that the bloc has reduced high-level contacts with Tbilisi amid strained relations. In its November 4 enlargement report, the European Commission pointed to Georgia’s “continued backsliding” and democratic deterioration, saying its EU integration “could resume” if the authorities “change course.” The Commission also warned that Georgia’s failure to address democratic concerns could put its visa-free regime with the EU at risk “more generally.” Meanwhile, Georgian officials have claimed that they seek to engage in "open and constructive dialogue" with the EU "on the basis of mutual respect." articles.title: Kazakhstan considers new rules to flag risks in online games
articles.summary: The Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s parliament, has proposed a bill that would introduce labeling requirements for online games, allow them to be checked and potentially blocked if they pose a threat. Digital platforms would also be required to introduce parental controls to restrict children’s ability to access or download games.
articles.body: The Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s parliament, has proposed a bill that would introduce labeling requirements for online games, allow them to be checked and potentially blocked if they pose a threat. Digital platforms would also be required to introduce parental controls to restrict children’s ability to access or download games. Notably, the bill is being discussed just days before the release of «Grand Theft Auto 6.» The criteria outlined in the bill include in-game purchases and chat functions. These provisions could also cover popular multiplayer games such as «Counter-Strike 2» and «Dota 2.» The proposal was discussed during Government Hour on Nov. 16, after Deputy Chair of the Kurultai Dinara Zakiyeva introduced the initiative. «It is envisaged that the safety of all digital and information products, including online games, will be ensured by introducing requirements for platforms to label and describe their digital risks, such as the ability to chat and in-game purchases. Furthermore, the proposal provides for a mechanism for mandatory verification by an authorized government body, monitoring for violations, and requiring the removal or blocking of information or digital products if a threat or risk associated with such a product, such as a game, is identified,» Zakiyeva said. It has yet to be announced which government body will be responsible for checking the games, what fines platforms could face and what criteria will be used to assess risks. Platform owners will be held responsible for all identified violations. Meanwhile, players who preordered a digital copy of “Grand Theft Auto 6» could begin preloading the game on Nov. 10, while its official release is scheduled for Nov. 19. The bill is unlikely to be passed before then. After the government issues its assessment, it will have to be reviewed by the Kurultai. It remains unclear how the regulations would apply to international digital stores and games that have already been released. The criteria outlined in the bill could also apply to other multiplayer games. «Counter-Strike 2» and «Dota 2» both feature in-game chat and purchases, exposing players to the risks that platforms would be required to flag. However, it remains unclear whether these provisions would cover such games or how they would apply to game developers and distribution platforms like Steam. Valve, the company behind both games and Steam, is also one of the largest foreign taxpayers in Kazakhstan .

Khanna proposes $1,700 Iran war refund checks for Americans
articles.summary: Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) on Monday proposed $1,700 refund checks to reimburse Americans for the economic impact of the Iran war. Khanna, a progressive and potential 2028 presidential contender, said on social media the checks would be sent to every American to cover higher gas, food and electricity prices caused by disruptions to oil transport…
articles.body: Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) on Monday proposed $1,700 refund checks to reimburse Americans for the economic impact of the Iran war. Khanna, a progressive and potential 2028 presidential contender, said on social media the checks would be sent to every American to cover higher gas, food and electricity prices caused by disruptions to oil transport routes due to the war. A frequent critic of the war, Khanna said Democrats were given an opportunity through their midterm victories. “I want to give every American family a $1,700 check to make them whole for the war in Iran,” Khanna said. The war has cost American households an average of $2,000 since its start, according to Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody’s Analytics. The cost of gas has risen to average highs of more than $4 per gallon, and it sits at $3.81 per gallon as of Monday afternoon. Diesel is about two dollars more expensive per gallon compared with a year ago. Khanna called on Democrats to vote on his measure almost immediately after taking over the chamber. The party won a larger-than-expected House majority and campaigned on its commitment to address affordability concerns. “Democrats have a chance to deliver. The first week in January, the House and Senate must pass a refund check to Americans,” Khanna wrote on social media. “Let’s put it on Trump’s desk.” President Trump has repeatedly said that higher prices are worth it to prevent a nuclear Iran. He said gas prices will fall once the war is over but has continued the conflict and recently said a deal to end the war was not needed. Khanna has been traveling the country campaigning for midterm candidates as he contemplates a presidential run. As a staunch progressive, he could fill the far-left lane in the Democratic primary field, potentially alongside another popular progressive — Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.). The California legislator has also called for Congress to eliminate all funding for the Iran war, which would effectively deny any ability for the Trump administration to continue operations. The cost of the war topped $47 billion in October. “I would stop the funding. The House and the Senate should stop the funding for any further actions in the Iran war. That’s what we did to stop the Vietnam War, and we need to stop this war in Iran,” Khanna said prior to the midterm elections.

articles.title: Crimean Bridge attack geared to disrupt peace talks — Russian lawmaker
articles.summary: "The Ukrainian aggressor’s attacks can be interpreted as yet again spitting on the large-scale peacemaking efforts by the American side, which is trying to stop bloodshed," Mikhail Sheremet stated
articles.body: SIMFEROPOL, November 16. /TASS/. By striking the Crimean Bridge, Ukraine is seeking to derail peace talks spearheaded by the United States, a Russian lawmaker told TASS. Crimea’s head Sergey Aksyonov said earlier that Ukrainian troops had struck the Crimean Bridge, temporarily halting motor traffic. "The Ukrainian aggressor’s aggressive attacks can be interpreted as yet again spitting on the large-scale peacemaking efforts by the American side, which is trying to stop bloodshed, and the Kiev junta’s open refusal from peaceful dialogue," said Mikhail Sheremet, a member of the Russian State Duma, or lower house of parliament, from Crimea. "This lunatic Zelensky wants to continue the war while staying in his comfortable hideout abroad, as the infrastructure of his dying country is being destroyed everywhere," he added. Another State Duma member from Crimea, Leonid Ivlev, also told TASS that he thinks that Zelensky doesn’t want to end the conflict and uses any steps toward peace agreements only as an opportunity to stockpile weapons and deliver more strikes on Russia. The current Kiev regime, acting on the instructions of its Western European sponsors, is ready to commit ever greater atrocities, the lawmaker stated. "And the Crimean Bridge stood, stands, and will continue to stand, despite the Ukrainian army’s attempts to strike it and the blather of talkative bloggers who, with a cynical eye, are calculating mythical damage percentages," he added.

articles.body: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 17. Iran and Oman noted the importance of maintaining stability in the region, the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported. The issue was discussed during the meeting between Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi and the Foreign Minister of Oman Badr Albusaidi in Muscat on Tuesday (November 17). During the meeting, the parties exchanged views on the importance of strengthening cooperation and consultations among regional countries to safeguard their shared interests. Discussions were also held regarding bilateral relations between Iran and Oman. The Iranian minister congratulated his counterpart on the occasion of the National Day of Oman and highlighted the significance of friendly relations and cooperation between the two countries across all sectors. The Iranian foreign minister arrived in Oman last night for an official visit.
